display.title: Good Morning, Hashem: Modeh Ani and the First Thank You of the Day
display.summary_short: Hashem watches over us all night and returns our neshamah fresh each morning, so the first thing we say is Modeh Ani, with a new Modeh Ani song.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi explains that Hashem is at our bedside all night long, welcomed into our room by the mezuzah on the doorpost, which never sleeps and guards us like a faithful soldier. When we wake up, Hashem is waiting for us to say good morning, and we do it with the twelve words of Modeh Ani. Each night we hand Hashem a tired neshamah, and each morning He gives it back fully charged and brand new, ready for davening, tzedakah, Torah and mitzvos. Uncle Yossi translates the words one by one, then plays a new song set to Modeh Ani. He ends with a lesson: Modeh Ani is the first thank you of the day, with many more to follow, so whenever someone does something for you, remember to say thank you.
display.lesson: Start the day by thanking Hashem with Modeh Ani, and get into the habit of saying thank you to everyone.
